Commentary.Commentary: Back for the chase. The players are out in the middle. Mujeeb Ur Rahman to bowl first. Tanzid Hasan and Parvez Hossain Emon to open for Bangladesh.
…THE RUN CHASE…

Bangladesh were tidy with the ball and backed it up with sharp work in the field. Shoriful Islam, Nasum Ahmed, and Mohammad Saifuddin were the standout performers, conceding just 60 runs across their combined 12 overs and picking up three key wickets. Rishad Hossain was a bit expensive but managed to strike twice, while Mustafizur Rahman had a rare off day. Chasing 148, Bangladesh will fancy their chances of taking an unassailable 2-0 lead in the series. But will it be smooth sailing, or can Afghanistan’s bowlers mount a spirited defense and make a game of it? We’ll find out shortly. Stay tuned for the second innings.

Another disciplined bowling performance from Bangladesh sees them restrict Afghanistan to a modest 147/5 in their allotted 20 overs. Asked to bat first, Afghanistan’s openers made a cautious start, putting on 55 for the first wicket. Both Ibrahim Zadran (38) and Sediqullah Atal (23) got off to promising starts but couldn’t convert them into big scores. The middle order struggled, with Rasooli and Tarakhil failing to make an impact. However, useful contributions from Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Mohammad Nabi, and Azmatullah Omarzai helped push the total beyond the 140-mark, giving Afghanistan something to bowl at.

FOUR! A boundary to end the innings! Yorker length delivery on the leg pole. Nabi manages to squeeze it through the backward square leg region and finds the ropes to close the innings. Afghanistan finish with 147/5.

Commentary.Commentary: All set now for the action to commence. The players and the umpires are in the middle. Ibrahim Zadran and Sediqullah Atal to open the innings for Afghanistan. It will be Shoriful Islam to begin with the ball for Bangladesh. Let's play...

Pitch Report - Rameez Raja and Andrew Leonard are at the pitch side. Rameez says that it is the same pitch as yesterday. He further shares that bowling second will help the spinners as the Afghans hit the hard length and keep it wicket to wicket. Tells that the bowlers need to be disciplined on this wicket and predicts that a score around 165-170 should be a par score.

Rashid Khan, the Afghanistan skipper, is happy to bat first as he feels that the spinners will get more help later in the game. Adds that the batters need to spend time on the crease and adjust to the conditions. Shares that they do not want to lose wickets in the first ten overs. Mentions that each game is important for them heading into the T20 World Cup, as they did not do well in the recent Tri-Series and the Asia Cup. Closes by adding the three changes with Fareed Ahmad, Sharafuddin Ashraf, and Mohammad Ishaq missing out for Wafiullah Tarakhil, Mustafizur Rahman, and Abdullah Ahmadzai.

Jaker Ali, the Bangladesh skipper, wins the toss and opts to bowl. Says they want to start well and use the same strategy as yesterday. Adds that it is difficult to play back-to-back games, but they are in a good frame of mind and up for the challenge. Closes by sharing that they have made two changes with Shoriful Islam and Mohammad Saifuddin coming in for Taskin Ahmed and Tanzim Hasan Sakib.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Tanzid Hasan, Parvez Hossain Emon, Saif Hassan, Jaker Ali(C)(WK), Nurul Hasan, Shamim Hossain, Mohammad Saifuddin (in for Tanzim Hasan Sakib), Mustafizur Rahman, Shoriful Islam (in for Taskin Ahmed), Rishad Hossain, Nasum Ahmed.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz(WK), Ibrahim Zadran, Sediqullah Atal, Darwish Rasooli, Wafiullah Tarakhil (on debut and in place of Mohammad Ishaq), Azmatullah Omarzai, Rashid Khan(C), Mohammad Nabi, Noor Ahmad, Mujeeb Ur Rahman (in for Sharafuddin Ashraf), Abdullah Ahmadzai (in for Fareed Ahmad).
Toss Update - Bangladesh have won the toss and opted to BOWL first.
So, can Afghanistan bounce back and make it 1-1, or will Bangladesh seal the series with a game to go? Let’s find out. Toss and team news coming up shortly. Stay tuned!

Bangladesh, on the other hand, did well with the ball, keeping Afghanistan to a below-par score. It was a collective bowling effort from the group, where Tanzim Hasan Sakib and Rishad Hossain were impressive, taking two each while attacking fifties from Tanzid Hasan and Parvez Hossain Emon laid a strong foundation, but they suffered a big collapse, losing six wickets for just 9 runs. Nurul Hasan and Rishad Hossain kept their calm and took their side home in a tense chase. The Tigers will hope to keep the momentum and take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the series.

In the opening game, Afghanistan struggled with the bat and managed to score 151/9 on the back of runs from Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Mohammad Nabi while Rashid Khan and Noor Ahmad staged a strong comeback with the ball after a poor start, but they eventually lost by 4 wickets in the penultimate over. The Afghans will hope to come hard and level the series with a game to go.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the second T20I in the three-match series between Afghanistan and Bangladesh, from the Sharjah Stadium in the UAE. Bangladesh started the series well with a nervy win, while Afghanistan will hope to bounce back and level the series.
…MATCHDAY…

The pressure gauge is firmly on red for Afghanistan as they head into Sharjah trailing 1-0 in this T20I series. After being outmanoeuvred in the opener, the key for the Afghans will be avoiding the kind of top-order wobble that saw them slump to 40 for 4, a deficit that proved too heavy to haul back. Only the timely fireworks from Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Mohammad Nabi, who put on an essential rescue act with a brace of 30-plus scores, prevented a total capitulation. While the pair showed fight, the margin for error has vanished, and Afghanistan must find a way to replicate that hitting while ensuring a steadier platform upfront. For Afghanistan to square the series, batting stability is must, and the onus falls heavily on Ibrahim Zadran, who has been their most dependable accumulator this season, to anchor the innings. Gurbaz will be relied upon for a quick start, while Nabi remains the designated finisher, capable of delivering a cameo at the death. With the ball, the wizardry of Rashid Khan remains their trump card, having delivered a brilliant spell in the first match. Supported by the pace and spin variation from Noor Ahmad, Fareed, and the all-round nous of Nabi, the attack certainly possesses the firepower to dismantle the Bangladeshi chase, provided they have a defendable score on the board. Bangladesh, conversely, arrive at the second game with confidence flowing, having delivered a thoroughly professional performance to take the lead. Their bowlers executed their plans tidily to restrict the Afghan power-hitters, and the subsequent chase was measured and calm. The foundation was brilliantly laid by the openers, Tanzid Hasan Tamim and Parvez Hossain Emon, whose fluent half-centuries took the sting completely out of the Afghan attack. With Saif Hassan providing a robust presence at number three, who failed to deliver in the first game, and depth secured by the tempo-controlling trio of Jaker Ali, Nurul Hasan, and Shamim Hossain, the Bangladeshi batting unit looks well and capable of handling any scenario. The momentum also lies with the Bangladesh attack, spearheaded by the pace duo of Taskin Ahmed, who is finding excellent rhythm, and Mustafizur Rahman, whose cutters and slower balls remain the ultimate weapon in the death overs. The spin-pace combination of Tanzim Hasan Sakib and Rishad Hossain proved effective in taking key wickets in the opener, adding genuine wicket-taking thrust to the side. Given the convincing nature of their first victory and the clinical execution across both departments, Bangladesh enters this contest as the favourites, and Afghanistan will require a serious lift in discipline and execution across the board just to force a decider.
